scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8103: URGENT!! Both halves of Campus 2 are OFF THE NETWORK --
nobody on the 10.5.0.x side or the 10.6.0.x side can reach their gateway
thingies at 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254. This all started after "a reload".
Something around the big switch must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could
someone look at it and get both floors online again!!! Thanks!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. sshswitch owns the Campus 2 L3 SVIs
  (10.5.0.254 for VLAN 5, 10.6.0.254 for VLAN 6) and they are UP. VLAN 5 hosts
  (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach 10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach
  10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / gateway outage on sshswitch that is
  not occurring (cf. kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down, where one SVI IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs
down so hosts cannot reach their gateways -- is NOT reproducible: the SVIs are up
(10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 answer), PC1 reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss, and PC3
reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the sshswitch SVIs are healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the host->gateway
paths for both VLANs, finds them working, checks the SVI state on sshswitch, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a down SVI -- restarting the switch or
blaming sshswitch's L3 interfaces to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully operational. Every Campus 2 host in both 10.5.0.0/24 (VLAN5, three PCs on switch4) and 10.6.0.0/24 (VLAN6, two PCs on switch4) successfully reaches its respective gateway (10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 on sshswitch). Inter-campus routing via OSPF is also working: Campus 2 PCs reach Campus 1 gateways (172.16.10.254, 172.16.20.254) and remote WAN subnets without loss. Campus 1 hosts reach their own gateways correctly.

The "after a reload" detail in the ticket is explained by the OSPF adjacency age (≈3–4 minutes old at time of investigation): sshswitch and router17 had recently restarted. During the startup script execution window — a matter of seconds — the VLAN 5/6 bridge-to-SVI path (eth0.5 → br_v5, eth0.6 → br_v6 on sshswitch) was not yet instantiated, momentarily making the gateways unreachable from switch4-connected PCs. This is the normal transient dark period of any device reload. Once the startup script completed, sshswitch's correct configuration — including the eth0.5/eth0.6 VLAN subinterface trunk fix (present in /hostlab/sshswitch.startup) — came up fully, and gateway reachability was restored within seconds.

No persistent misconfiguration, interface error, routing black-hole, or VLAN miswiring was found on any device. No corrective action is needed; the lab is in a healthy, converged state.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs (10.5.0.254 / 10.6.0.254) are up and answer hosts with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states the sshswitch SVIs (10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254) are reachable from Campus 2 hosts and notes hosts reach their gateways (and remote prefixes) without loss, matching the baseline healthy condition.

The investigation log contains multiple, concrete reachability and control-plane checks (pings from PCs to SVIs, ip neigh, OSPF neighbors, running config, bond/interface status) that support the agent's conclusion that the SVIs are up and the report was not reproducible; the agent's inference that a recent reload caused a short transient outage is plausible and consistent with the OSPF adjacency ages.
